tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Dismissal of Charges or Disposition (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1401)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest or dismissed charge

controllingAuthority.summary: On a verified petition to the court in which the proceeding occurred or would have occurred, the court may expunge records of an arrest, a charge that was dismissed, or a disposition where the person was not convicted, provided at least 180 days have passed, no formal charges are pending, and no disposition under § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 was entered to any charge arising from the incident, including to a different or lesser charge. Expungement classifies the record at the Division of Criminal Investigation so it is not disseminated except to criminal justice agencies for criminal justice purposes; the court file is sealed and a certified order is transmitted to DCI.

exclusions: Any disposition under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 entered to any charge resulting from the incident, including a disposition to a different or lesser charge.
Formal charges pending against the person at the time the petition is filed.

Records that are not maintained in the state central repository at the Division of Criminal Investigation, including investigatory files of any local, state or federal criminal justice agency used solely for criminal justice purposes.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

waitingPeriods.condition: Arrest with no charges filed, or charges filed and not resulting in conviction
waitingPeriods.duration: At least 180 days since the arrest

waitingPeriods.condition: Charges dismissed by the prosecutor or the court
waitingPeriods.duration: At least 180 days since the date the charges were dismissed

geography.venue: The court in which the proceeding occurred, or would have occurred. Where no charges were ever filed there is no existing case, and the petition goes to the court that would have had jurisdiction over the matter.

destination.name: The Wyoming court in which the proceeding occurred or would have occurred
destination.detail: File the verified petition and the proposed Order for Expungement with the clerk of that court. Serve the prosecuting attorney. No filing fee applies under § 7-13-1401. On grant the court seals the file and transmits a certified copy of the order to the Division of Criminal Investigation.

components.notes: Petition for Expungement (W.S. 7-13-1401). Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form, so this is drafted. Caption the underlying criminal case where one exists, with the participant identified as the defendant. Where no charges were filed and there is no case number, the petition opens a new matter and the clerk assigns the number. Cite only § 7-13-1401; do not blend the three Wyoming expungement statutes in one petition.

Order for Expungement, which the Wyoming Judicial Branch expects the petitioner to have ready for the judge's signature. The order directs that the court file be placed under seal, available for inspection only by order of the court, and that a certified copy be transmitted to the Division of Criminal Investigation. The order is proposed and is generated unexecuted: its findings, its date, the judge's signature block and every clerk or court execution field are left blank, and nothing in it asserts that the court has acted. It is prepared so it is available to the court; whether it goes in with the initial filing or is brought later is that court's filing practice.
Verification block. Section 7-13-1401 requires the petition to be verified by the petitioner; this is not optional.
Certificate of service on the prosecuting attorney. The 20-day objection window runs from service, so the service date governs when an order may issue.

Filing, service and timing sheet: call the clerk about local templates and formatting before finalizing; file; serve the prosecuting attorney; no order may issue before 20 days after service; if the prosecutor objects the court sets a hearing; if no objection the court may summarily enter the order on finding eligibility. No civil summons and no praecipe are required on this route under the statewide statutes and published guidance, and neither is generated. The clerk call covers local filing mechanics only — cover sheet, copy count, electronic or paper filing, chambers copy, and whether the proposed order goes in with the initial filing or is brought later — because Wyoming publishes no statewide form for either document and there is no local template outside Casper Municipal Court that this route uses.

rules.filing: File the verified Petition for Expungement and the proposed Order for Expungement with the clerk of the court in which the proceeding occurred or would have occurred. Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form and no statewide proposed-order template, so both documents are drafted and are complete as drafted. Call that clerk about that court's own filing mechanics — cover sheet, copy count, electronic or paper filing, whether a chambers copy is wanted, and whether the proposed order is submitted with the initial filing or brought later — not about whether the document itself is right.
rules.notice: The prosecuting attorney reviews the petition. No order may be granted before the expiration of 20 days after service on the prosecuting attorney. If the prosecutor objects the court sets a hearing; if no objection is filed the court may summarily enter the order on finding the petitioner eligible.
rules.service: Serve the verified petition on the prosecuting attorney and file proof of service. The Division of Criminal Investigation is not a service recipient on this track.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and verifies the petition. Verification by the petitioner is required by statute.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute; confirm with the clerk of the filing court whether that court requires the verification to be sworn before a notary.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any deferred disposition under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 arising from the incident, including a disposition entered to a different or lesser charge — this track is closed and the participant is routed to § 7-13-1501 where the underlying matter was a misdemeanor.
A completed felony deferral. Section 7-13-1401 is barred by the deferral and § 7-13-1502 by its terms requires a conviction, so there may be no Wyoming route at all. Stop and refer to a lawyer.
The prosecuting attorney files an objection, or the court sets a contested hearing.
Criminal charges are pending against the participant.
Facts indicating human trafficking or coercion, which route to the § 6-2-708 vacatur outside this track.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration.
Immigration consequences.
Federal, tribal or out-of-state records.
Records of a juvenile matter, which are handled under Wyo. Stat. § 14-6-241 and § 14-6-440 outside this track.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The cleanest track in Wyoming: no filing fee, no substantial-danger finding, no lifetime cap, a 180-day wait, and a summary-entry path where the prosecuting attorney does not object. The review approved it for implementation without limitation, and identifies it as the volume product for the state. Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form, so the track is a custom pleading; that is the settled classification for the jurisdiction rather than a gap.

limitations.statement: Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. County clerks, municipal courts and circuit courts may have local templates or formatting requirements. Call the clerk of the court where the petition will be filed before finalizing, and use a local template where one exists. Never invent a statewide form number.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Misdemeanors (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1501)

controllingAuthority.summary: A person who has pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a misdemeanor may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. The waiting period is at least five years for non-status offenses and at least one year for status offenses as defined by § 7-1-107(b)(iii), measured from expiration of the terms of sentence including probation and any court-ordered program. The offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm; a health care provider convicted of a § 6-2-313 offense against a patient in their care is ineligible. The court must find the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Per the Wyoming Judicial Branch, the section includes cases of deferred adjudication and cases where the charge was later dismissed.

exclusions: Misdemeanors involving the use or attempted use of a firearm.
A health care provider who pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or was convicted of, an offense punishable under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-313 committed against a patient under that provider's care.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1501; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Felony convictions, which are handled under § 7-13-1502.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least 5 years since the expiration of the terms of the sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation or completion of any program ordered by the court

waitingPeriods.condition: Status offense as defined by Wyo. Stat. § 7-1-107(b)(iii)
waitingPeriods.duration: At least 1 year since the expiration of the terms of the sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation or completion of any program ordered by the court

destination.name: The Wyoming convicting court
destination.detail: File the verified petition and the proposed Order for Expungement with the clerk of the convicting court and pay the $100 filing fee per petition. tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Felonies (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1502)

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a felony, or of felonies subject to expungement under the section arising out of the same occurrence or related course of events, may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. At least ten years must have passed since expiration of the terms of sentence including probation; any court-ordered program must be complete and court-ordered restitution paid in full; the petitioner must have no other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction; the offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm except certain Title 23 offenses; and the offense must not appear on the statutory exclusion list. The court must find eligibility and that the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Under subsection (m) the expungement restores any rights removed as a result of the conviction.

exclusions: Violent felonies under Wyo. Stat. § 6-1-104(a)(xii).
Aggravated homicide by vehicle; drug-induced homicide.
Sexual assault and related sexual offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-2-301 through 6-2-320.
Certain domestic battery offenses; child abuse; endangering children with controlled substances; incest; sexual exploitation of children.
Aggravated assault or battery on a corrections or detention officer; disarming a peace officer; escape from official detention and violent or armed escape.
Bribery.
Weapons offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-8-101 and 6-8-102.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under Wyo. Stat. §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
Felonies involving the use or attempted use of a firearm, except certain Title 23 offenses.
Any petitioner who has previously pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a felony other than the felony or felonies being expunged.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1502; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Is the Lynch citation accurate? The internal reference cites a Wyoming Supreme Court decision at docket S-25-0140, reported as a 2026 case, for the proposition that § 7-13-1502 requires an actual felony conviction and that a completed deferral producing a dismissal is not one. A search surfaced a different Lynch matter from 2024 on an unrelated issue. The proposition is consistent with the statutory text, which opens with 'a person convicted of a felony', but the citation could not be confirmed.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Which unpublished local filing preferences apply in the court where this petition will be filed: local cover sheet, copy count, electronic versus paper filing, filing method, chambers copy, whether the proposed Order for Expungement is submitted with the initial filing or later, any unpublished local template, any unpublished additional service document, and other court-specific filing mechanics. This is the narrowed remainder of the original packet-assembly question, which asked which Wyoming courts publish local expungement templates. The published half is answered: Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form and no statewide proposed-order template, and Casper Municipal Court is the only publicly identified local-form exception, whose packets bind that court alone. What remains is unpublished preference, which is filing mechanics rather than the legal document, so it is release-level and does not block generation of the statewide verified petition and proposed order. It is owned by rcap-wy-local-template-and-handout-survey, which remains open: no Wyoming county has been telephoned and the survey must not be recorded as complete. Escalation: if a county's answer changes the statewide legal document rather than only how it is filed, that exact issue returns to legal design before release.

provenance.sourceStatement: Which Wyoming courts publish local expungement templates? Not surveyed. Build blocker for packet assembly, resolvable by a clerk survey across the 23 counties.

tracks._limitationsNote: Every limitation is classified. Only legal_design_blocker withholds a track and must name the undetermined element.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Approved for implementation with limitations and a manual-review gate. Three facts drive that: the exclusion list is long and statute-specific, the other-felony bar looks at the whole record, and the restoration-of-rights effect under subsection (m) makes this the highest-value single filing in Wyoming, which means it should not be attempted on thin facts. The ninety-day objection window also makes a Wyoming felony petition a four-month engagement at minimum, and the participant should be told so.

limitations.statement: The § 7-13-1502 exclusion list is long and statute-specific and is not encoded. Do not offer this track without attorney review of whether the felony appears on the list.
